item.content:encoded:
The Paul Hamlyn Foundation (PHF) Teacher Development Fund supports partnerships between schools and arts or cultural organisations that use arts-based approaches to improve teaching, learning and equity for children.

The fund is designed around the belief that high-quality arts-based learning can help create more equitable classrooms where children can learn, participate and thrive.

Funding Amount and Duration

Successful applicants can receive up to £165,000 per application.

Projects are expected to run for two academic years, giving schools and arts organisations sufficient time to develop professional learning, test arts-based approaches in classrooms, evaluate their impact and build sustainable changes in teaching and learning.

What Does the Teacher Development Fund Support?

The fund focuses on developing teachers’ skills and confidence in using arts-based approaches in education. Supported projects should contribute to more equitable learning environments, particularly for pupils experiencing systemic inequity.

The programme aims to:

  • Improve access to learning for pupils experiencing systemic inequity.
  • Strengthen collaboration between schools and arts or cultural organisations.
  • Provide high-quality professional learning for teachers.
  • Enable teachers and artist practitioners to learn from and work alongside one another in classrooms.
  • Build evidence and practical knowledge about how arts-based learning can improve equity.
  • Encourage sustainable improvements in teaching and learning that continue beyond the project period.

Who Can Lead an Application?

Either of the following can act as the lead applicant:

  1. A primary school, or
  2. An arts or cultural organisation.

However, applications must be based on a strong partnership between schools and arts or cultural organisations.

Each project must involve:

  • A minimum of six schools.
  • A maximum of ten schools.
  • At least one arts or cultural organisation.
  • At least two teachers and one senior leader from each participating school, although some flexibility may be available for small or rural schools.

Eligible Schools and Organisations

Participating schools must operate in the state sector and can include:

  • Mainstream primary schools.
  • Specialist SEND settings.
  • Alternative Provision settings.
  • Schools working with primary-age children.

Teachers working with Nursery and Reception classes in primary schools may also be included.

Eligible arts organisations can include:

  • Charities.
  • Community organisations.
  • Social enterprises.
  • Not-for-profit companies active in the arts and culture sector.

What Will Funded Projects Work On?

The Teacher Development Fund expects projects to develop a structured professional learning programme over two academic years.

Key areas include:

  • Equity: Improving learning opportunities and outcomes for pupils.
  • Professional learning: Developing teachers’ knowledge, skills and confidence.
  • Arts-based approaches: Integrating creative and arts-based methods into classroom teaching.
  • Curriculum: Exploring how arts-based approaches can enhance curriculum delivery.
  • Formative evaluation: Learning from the implementation of the project and using evidence to improve practice.
  • Spreading practice: Sharing learning and effective approaches beyond participating schools.
  • Cohort learning: Creating opportunities for participating schools and practitioners to learn together.
  • Community of practice: Building longer-term networks for collaboration and shared learning.

What Makes a Strong Partnership?

The foundation highlights several characteristics associated with effective partnerships and practice.

These include:

  • Anti-racism.
  • Intersectionality.
  • Effective professional learning.
  • Meaningful involvement of school leaders.
  • Strong roles for artist practitioners.
  • Enquiry-driven and reflective practice.

Applicants should therefore demonstrate that the proposed partnership is more than a simple relationship between a funder, school and arts organisation. The partners should be able to show how they will work together, learn together and create meaningful improvements in teaching and learning.

Deadline

The deadline to apply for the Teacher Development Fund is 11 November 2026 at 12 noon.

Applicants should allow sufficient time to establish the required partnerships, develop the project approach, clarify participating schools and prepare the application before the deadline.

How to Apply

Applications are submitted through the Paul Hamlyn Foundation’s application system.

Applicants should also review the foundation’s detailed eligibility guidance and FAQs before applying.

Click HERE to read more and apply.

Conclusion

The Teacher Development Fund provides substantial support for schools and arts or cultural organisations seeking to use arts-based learning to create more equitable educational environments. With funding of up to £165,000, a two-academic-year project period and a strong emphasis on teacher development, partnership working, evaluation and sustainable change, the opportunity is particularly relevant to organisations with established experience in arts education and schools committed to improving outcomes for children experiencing systemic inequity.

item.content:encoded:
Are you a Master’s student passionate about sustainability, corporate social responsibility, social impact, philanthropy, and project management? L’Oréal is offering an exciting 12-month apprenticeship opportunity with La Roche-Posay, one of its leading dermatological beauty brands, beginning in January 2027.

The La Roche-Posay Sustainability Apprentice – Junior Project Manager Sustainable Development & Social Impact opportunity offers students the chance to gain practical experience working on environmental sustainability, social-impact initiatives, philanthropic programmes, communications, and brand-cause projects within one of the world’s largest beauty companies.

The apprenticeship is based in Île-de-France, France, with the position associated with the La Roche-Posay/L’Oréal teams in the Paris region.

Successful candidates will receive €1,700 per month, partial public transportation reimbursement, one remote-working day per week, paid leave, access to L’Oréal’s learning platform, preferential employee purchasing benefits, and other workplace perks.

If you are interested in building a career in sustainability, corporate responsibility, project management, communications, social impact, or responsible business, this opportunity could provide valuable international corporate experience.

Opportunity Overview

  • Organisation: L’Oréal Groupe
  • Brand: La Roche-Posay
  • Division: L’Oréal Dermatological Beauty
  • Position: Junior Project Manager Sustainable Development & Social Impact / Sustainability Apprentice
  • Opportunity type: 12-month apprenticeship
  • Location: Île-de-France, France
  • Work arrangement: Full-time, with one remote-working day per week
  • Start date: January 2027
  • End date: December 2027
  • Monthly remuneration: €1,700
  • Public transportation: 75% of public transport costs covered
  • Paid leave: 1 day per month
  • Language: English mandatory; French highly desired
  • Application deadline: The posting is dated 31 August 2026. The vacancy page provided does not state a specific closing date, so applicants should apply as soon as possible while the position remains available.

About the L’Oréal La Roche-Posay Apprenticeship

L’Oréal is offering this apprenticeship to students who want to combine professional development with meaningful work in sustainability and social impact.

The role goes beyond traditional administrative or internship responsibilities. The selected apprentice will participate in projects covering three interconnected areas:

  1. La Roche-Posay Foundation and philanthropy
  2. Environmental sustainability and sustainable development
  3. Social impact and brand-cause initiatives

This means the successful candidate will gain exposure to environmental, social and philanthropic programmes while learning how a major international brand develops, implements, communicates and measures its impact.

The apprenticeship is particularly relevant for students interested in how large companies integrate sustainability and social responsibility into their business strategies.

Why La Roche-Posay?

La Roche-Posay is a leading dermo-cosmetic skincare brand within L’Oréal Dermatological Beauty.

The brand’s approach is based on the principle that health is the future of beauty, connecting scientific research, skincare innovation and social responsibility.

Through this apprenticeship, students will have an opportunity to contribute to initiatives designed to create positive environmental and social outcomes while gaining an understanding of how sustainability operates within an international corporate environment.

The role also provides exposure to external organisations, including NGOs and associations, as well as internal teams responsible for marketing, communications, research and innovation, and sustainable development.

Key Areas of Responsibility

1. La Roche-Posay Foundation and Philanthropy

One of the major components of the apprenticeship involves supporting the La Roche-Posay Foundation.

The apprentice will contribute to the development and implementation of philanthropic programmes supported by the Foundation.

Responsibilities include:

  • Contributing to the development of philanthropic programmes.
  • Supporting the deployment and implementation of Foundation initiatives.
  • Helping communicate philanthropic programmes internally.
  • Supporting external communications about Foundation activities.
  • Helping increase awareness of the Foundation’s programmes.
  • Supporting the team with day-to-day philanthropic activities.

This part of the role is particularly relevant to students interested in philanthropy, nonprofit partnerships, social impact, communications and programme management.

2. Environmental Sustainability and Sustainable Development

The apprentice will also contribute to La Roche-Posay’s environmental sustainability transformation.

This involves supporting initiatives designed to strengthen the brand’s sustainability commitments and communicating its environmental progress.

Potential responsibilities include:

  • Contributing to sustainable transformation projects.
  • Supporting sustainability initiatives.
  • Helping pilot key environmental initiatives.
  • Developing content related to sustainability.
  • Creating campaign assets.
  • Supporting internal communications about environmental initiatives.
  • Supporting external communications about sustainability achievements.
  • Helping communicate the brand’s environmental commitments to wider audiences.

This aspect of the position makes the opportunity particularly attractive for students interested in ESG, sustainability, climate action, corporate responsibility and responsible business.

3. Social Impact and Brand Cause

The third major area involves social initiatives, particularly programmes connected with oncology and support for cancer patients.

The apprentice will contribute to the development and implementation of social programmes and help communicate their impact.

Responsibilities include:

  • Supporting the development of programmes dedicated to oncology.
  • Contributing to initiatives supporting cancer patients.
  • Helping pilot social-impact initiatives.
  • Creating communication and campaign content.
  • Developing campaign assets.
  • Supporting internal communication.
  • Supporting external communication.
  • Helping communicate the achievements and impact of social programmes.

This gives the successful candidate an opportunity to understand how a global consumer brand can use its platform and resources to address societal issues.

Daily Responsibilities

In addition to the three principal areas of responsibility, the apprentice will provide day-to-day support to the Sustainability, Brand Cause and Philanthropic Foundation team.

This means the position can involve a variety of activities rather than being restricted to one narrow area.

The successful candidate should therefore be comfortable managing multiple priorities, collaborating with different stakeholders and adapting to changing project requirements.

What You Will Learn

The apprenticeship is designed to provide both professional and personal development.

According to the vacancy, the experience will provide a global and strategic understanding of the brand’s commitments to sustainability and social impact.

During the 12 months, the apprentice can gain exposure to:

  • Corporate social responsibility.
  • Sustainable development.
  • Environmental sustainability.
  • Social impact.
  • Philanthropy.
  • Project management.
  • Campaign development.
  • Corporate communications.
  • Stakeholder engagement.
  • Brand-cause initiatives.
  • NGO and association partnerships.
  • Environmental and social challenges.
  • International business operations.
  • Cross-functional collaboration.

The apprentice will also work with multiple departments and external stakeholders, creating opportunities to understand how sustainability projects are developed and implemented within a multinational organisation.

Collaboration and Stakeholder Exposure

One of the strongest features of this apprenticeship is its cross-functional nature.

The successful candidate will work with La Roche-Posay teams and L’Oréal Dermatological Beauty while interacting with external stakeholders such as NGOs and associations.

The role also provides interaction with internal departments including:

  • Marketing.
  • Communications.
  • Research and Innovation.
  • Sustainable Development.
  • Impact and Sustainability.

This type of exposure can be valuable for someone seeking a future career in project management, sustainability consulting, corporate responsibility, ESG, communications or social-impact strategy.

Who Is L’Oréal Looking For?

L’Oréal is looking for a Master’s student who is genuinely interested in sustainability, CSR, social responsibility and philanthropy.

The ideal candidate should demonstrate more than academic qualifications. The company is also interested in curiosity, communication ability, initiative, creativity and the capacity to work independently.

Key qualities and skills include:

  • Clear interest in corporate social responsibility.
  • Interest in sustainable development.
  • Interest in social responsibility.
  • Interest in philanthropy.
  • Curiosity about brand environments.
  • Curiosity about societal issues.
  • Results-oriented mindset.
  • Strong attention to detail.
  • Excellent written communication skills.
  • Excellent oral communication skills.
  • Strong interpersonal skills.
  • Data-analysis skills.
  • Proactivity.
  • Ability to work autonomously.
  • Creativity.
  • Entrepreneurial spirit.
  • Open-mindedness.

Language Requirements

English proficiency is mandatory for this position.

Strong English communication skills are therefore essential.

French proficiency is highly desired, making knowledge of French an important advantage for candidates working in France and interacting with French-speaking colleagues or stakeholders.

Candidates who do not speak French may therefore still be considered based on the vacancy’s stated requirements, but French language skills could strengthen an application.

Academic Requirements

Applicants must be:

  • Master’s students.
  • Studying at an engineering school, business school or university.
  • Available for a 12-month apprenticeship.
  • Available from January 2027 through December 2027.
  • Comfortable working in an English-speaking environment.

The opportunity is therefore specifically structured for students who are undertaking or entering a Master’s-level programme that supports an apprenticeship arrangement.

What Does L’Oréal Offer?

The apprenticeship provides a combination of financial compensation, professional development and employee benefits.

Monthly remuneration

The selected apprentice will receive:

€1,700 per month

This provides financial support throughout the 12-month apprenticeship.

Transportation support

L’Oréal will cover 75% of public transportation costs, helping reduce commuting expenses for the successful candidate.

Remote working

The position provides:

One day of remote working per week

This gives the apprentice some flexibility while maintaining regular interaction with the team.

Paid leave

The listed benefits include:

One day of paid leave per month

Learning and development

Apprentices will have unlimited access to L’Oréal’s My Learning platform.

This can support continuous professional development and allow participants to build additional skills during their placement.

Employee purchasing benefits

The opportunity also provides access to preferential prices through L’Oréal’s internal online store.

Other benefits include Friends & Family sales.

Depending on the campus, additional facilities may include amenities such as gyms and concierge services.

A Potential Pathway to a Permanent Career

Another particularly interesting feature of the opportunity is L’Oréal’s emphasis on developing early-career talent.

The company states that approximately 70% of its entry-level positions are filled by former interns and apprentices.

This does not guarantee a permanent position after the apprenticeship, but it demonstrates that apprenticeships can serve as an important entry point into the L’Oréal Group.

For students who perform strongly and demonstrate the skills, attitude and potential required by the organisation, the apprenticeship could therefore provide valuable exposure to future career opportunities.

L’Oréal’s Internship and Apprenticeship Environment

L’Oréal reports strong satisfaction among its interns.

According to the company’s internal satisfaction survey from June 2026:

  • 88% of interns said they were proud to work at L’Oréal.
  • 87% recommended L’Oréal for an internship.

These figures reflect the company’s stated internal survey results and highlight its emphasis on providing a positive early-career experience.

Recruitment Process

Applicants should be prepared for a two-stage recruitment process.

Stage 1: Recruiter Interview

The first stage is a 30-minute recruiter interview.

This stage is designed to introduce yourself and discuss the position and the L’Oréal Group.

Applicants should be prepared to explain:

  • Their academic background.
  • Why they are interested in L’Oréal.
  • Why they are interested in La Roche-Posay.
  • Why sustainability and social impact matter to them.
  • Their relevant skills.
  • Their career objectives.
  • Their availability for the January 2027 start date.

Stage 2: Interview With the Potential Manager

The second stage is a 45-minute meeting with the potential future manager.

This discussion is expected to focus more deeply on the missions of the position.

Candidates should therefore be prepared to demonstrate how their previous academic, professional, volunteer or project experience relates to sustainability, project management, communications, data analysis and social-impact initiatives.

Why This Opportunity Could Be Valuable

This apprenticeship can be particularly valuable because it combines several career areas within one position.

A successful apprentice can gain experience in:

  1. Project management — supporting and piloting sustainability and social-impact initiatives.
  2. Sustainability — participating in environmental transformation projects.
  3. CSR — understanding how corporate responsibility programmes operate.
  4. Social impact — contributing to programmes supporting communities and cancer patients.
  5. Philanthropy — supporting Foundation programmes.
  6. Communications — developing content and campaign materials.
  7. Stakeholder management — interacting with internal and external partners.
  8. Data analysis — applying analytical skills to sustainability and social-impact work.
  9. International business — gaining experience within a multinational corporation.
  10. Cross-functional teamwork — collaborating with marketing, communications, research and sustainability teams.

For a student planning a long-term career in sustainability, consulting, project management, CSR, ESG or corporate strategy, this combination can be particularly useful.

Important Information for International Applicants

The position is located in France, specifically in the Île-de-France region.

Applicants should carefully consider the practical requirements of undertaking a French apprenticeship, including whether their Master’s programme and immigration/work status allow them to participate in the apprenticeship arrangement.

The vacancy itself specifies that applicants must be Master’s students and available for a 12-month apprenticeship from January to December 2027.

International candidates should therefore verify their eligibility for the relevant French apprenticeship and student/work authorization requirements before making arrangements.

AI at L’Oréal

L’Oréal also highlights its approach to artificial intelligence through its AI Charter.

The company describes AI as a tool that can support innovation while emphasising that technology should serve people.

L’Oréal states that it assesses the social, environmental and societal impacts of its AI systems and seeks to mitigate potential or actual harm.

This reflects the company’s broader position that economic and environmental performance should be considered together.

How to Apply

Interested candidates should apply through the official L’Oréal careers platform.

The application page is available through the job listing:

Apply for the La Roche-Posay Sustainability Apprenticeship

Applicants should carefully review their CV and application before submitting.

L’Oréal notes that candidates can apply to up to three jobs within a rolling 30-day period.

The company also states that an application cannot be withdrawn once submitted, so applicants should make sure they select positions that genuinely match their career interests.

Applicants are also advised not to create another account using a different email address, as doing so could result in the account being merged and the application record being deleted.

Application Tips

To improve your application, consider the following:

1. Tailor your CV to sustainability

Do not submit a generic CV if you can avoid it.

Highlight experience related to:

  • Sustainability.
  • CSR.
  • Project management.
  • Research.
  • Data analysis.
  • Communications.
  • Social-impact initiatives.
  • NGOs or community projects.
  • Events and campaigns.
  • Stakeholder coordination.

2. Demonstrate measurable achievements

Where possible, show what you accomplished rather than simply listing your responsibilities.

For example, instead of only saying that you “supported projects,” explain what you coordinated, improved, delivered or achieved.

3. Highlight project-management skills

Because the position includes piloting initiatives, candidates should demonstrate their ability to plan, coordinate and deliver projects.

Examples could include academic projects, professional assignments, volunteer programmes, campaigns or community initiatives.

4. Show genuine interest in sustainability

Research La Roche-Posay and L’Oréal before applying.

Be prepared to explain why sustainability, social impact and responsible business are important to you.

5. Prepare for the recruiter interview

The 30-minute recruiter interview is an opportunity to demonstrate motivation and fit.

Prepare a clear introduction explaining:

  • Who you are.
  • What you study.
  • Your relevant experience.
  • Why you want this apprenticeship.
  • Why L’Oréal interests you.
  • Why La Roche-Posay interests you.
  • What you hope to learn.

6. Prepare examples for the manager interview

For the 45-minute manager interview, prepare specific examples demonstrating:

  • Leadership.
  • Initiative.
  • Problem-solving.
  • Communication.
  • Teamwork.
  • Data analysis.
  • Project coordination.
  • Attention to detail.
  • Working independently.

Important Dates

The apprenticeship is scheduled to run for 12 months:

January 2027 – December 2027

The job posting is dated:

31 August 2026

Application deadline

No specific closing deadline is stated on the vacancy page provided.

Because recruitment may close once a suitable candidate is selected, interested students should avoid waiting until the last minute and should apply while the vacancy remains open.

About L’Oréal Groupe

L’Oréal is one of the world’s largest beauty companies, with operations in more than 150 countries.

The company has a portfolio of international brands across four major divisions:

  • Consumer Products.
  • Professional Products.
  • Dermatological Beauty.
  • Luxury.

La Roche-Posay operates within the Dermatological Beauty division.

The Group describes its mission as creating beauty that moves, inspires and unites, while combining technology, science and natural inspiration to provide inclusive, responsible and forward-looking beauty.

L’Oréal also states that equal opportunity and diversity are important values within the Group and that it considers applications regardless of characteristics such as gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, social or cultural origins, health status, age or religion.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the L’Oréal La Roche-Posay Sustainability Apprenticeship?

It is a 12-month apprenticeship focused on sustainable development, environmental sustainability, social impact, philanthropy and brand-cause initiatives at La Roche-Posay, a L’Oréal Dermatological Beauty brand.

When does the apprenticeship start?

The apprenticeship starts in January 2027.

When does it end?

The programme is scheduled to run until December 2027.

How much does the apprenticeship pay?

The advertised remuneration is €1,700 per month.

Where is the apprenticeship located?

The opportunity is in Île-de-France, France, with the vacancy description referencing the Levallois-Perret area.

Is English required?

Yes. English proficiency is mandatory.

Is French required?

French is highly desired, although the listing specifically identifies English as mandatory.

Who can apply?

The position is aimed at Master’s students studying at an engineering school, business school or university who are available for a 12-month apprenticeship beginning in January 2027.

Is this a remote position?

No. The position is not fully remote. L’Oréal offers one remote-working day per week.

Does L’Oréal cover transportation?

Yes. The advertised benefit is coverage of 75% of public transportation costs.

Is there a fixed application deadline?

No specific closing date is provided in the vacancy information supplied. The listing is dated 31 August 2026, so candidates should apply as early as possible.

Can applicants apply for multiple L’Oréal positions?

Yes. L’Oréal states that applicants can apply to up to three jobs within a rolling 30-day period.

Can an application be withdrawn?

According to the vacancy notice, applicants cannot withdraw an application once they have applied.

Final Thoughts

The L’Oréal La Roche-Posay Sustainability Apprenticeship 2027 is a strong opportunity for Master’s students who want practical experience at the intersection of sustainability, social impact, philanthropy, communications and project management.

Rather than focusing on a single responsibility, the apprenticeship exposes the successful candidate to environmental sustainability, social programmes and philanthropic initiatives while providing opportunities to collaborate with marketing, communications, research, innovation and sustainable-development professionals.

The €1,700 monthly remuneration, transportation support, weekly remote-working option, paid leave, learning platform and other benefits make the opportunity particularly attractive for eligible students seeking international professional experience.

Perhaps most importantly, the position can provide a valuable foundation for a career in sustainability, ESG, CSR, project management, social impact, responsible business, corporate communications or consulting.

Students who meet the Master’s-level academic requirement, can commit to the January–December 2027 apprenticeship period and have a genuine interest in sustainability and social impact should consider applying early.

Apply through the official L’Oréal careers platform while the vacancy remains open.

item.content:encoded:
The Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) Fellowships provide prestigious opportunities for individuals seeking to deepen their understanding of international affairs, foreign policy, diplomacy, national security, and global policymaking. Designed to give selected fellows meaningful exposure to new environments and policymaking settings, CFR’s fellowship programs can provide an important platform for professionals committed to building long-term careers in foreign policy.

Through its diverse portfolio of domestic and overseas fellowships, the Council on Foreign Relations connects talented professionals with opportunities to gain practical experience, broaden their perspectives, engage with experts, and contribute to discussions surrounding some of the world’s most important international challenges.

For U.S. citizens with a demonstrated commitment to a career in foreign policy, these fellowships can provide an opportunity to step outside their existing professional environment and gain direct exposure to policymaking institutions, international affairs research, diplomacy, journalism, technology policy, nuclear security, and other areas relevant to America’s engagement with the world.

What Are Council on Foreign Relations Fellowships?

The Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) Fellowships are specialized fellowship opportunities intended to broaden the perspectives and professional experiences of individuals working toward careers in foreign policy and international affairs.

According to the information provided by CFR, selected fellows can gain exposure to a new environment in one of several settings, including:

  • A policymaking environment
  • The Council on Foreign Relations itself
  • An overseas professional or policy environment
  • Specialized institutions and organizations connected to foreign policy
  • Professional settings related to journalism, technology diplomacy, national security, and international affairs

The objective is not simply to provide a temporary professional placement. CFR describes its fellowships as unique and transformational opportunities through which fellows can develop broader perspectives on foreign affairs.

This makes the programs particularly relevant to professionals who want to expand their understanding beyond their current area of work and gain exposure to the complex processes through which international policy is researched, debated, developed, and implemented.

Why CFR Fellowships Are Important

International affairs increasingly require professionals who understand how different countries, institutions, political systems, economic interests, security priorities, technological developments, and global challenges interact.

A professional working in foreign policy may need to understand diplomacy. A journalist covering international affairs may need deeper knowledge of national security. A technology professional may need to understand how artificial intelligence and emerging technologies affect international relations. Likewise, policymakers may need exposure to academic research, international institutions, media perspectives, and overseas policy environments.

CFR’s fellowship programs are structured around this type of professional development.

By placing fellows in new environments, the programs can expose participants to perspectives and experiences that may not be available through their existing professional roles.

International Affairs Fellowship Programs Overseas

One of the major components of the CFR fellowship portfolio is its collection of overseas fellowship programs.

These programs provide opportunities for selected fellows to gain international exposure while examining foreign policy issues from a different national or regional perspective.

The overseas programs listed in the information provided include:

1. International Affairs Fellowship in Canada

The International Affairs Fellowship in Canada provides an overseas pathway for fellows interested in developing their understanding of international affairs through exposure to the Canadian environment.

Canada is an important partner of the United States, and professional exposure in the country can provide insights into bilateral relations, diplomacy, international cooperation, security, trade, and broader North American affairs.

The fellowship is therefore particularly relevant to professionals whose interests intersect with U.S.-Canadian relations or broader international policy questions.

2. International Affairs Fellowship in India

The International Affairs Fellowship in India provides an opportunity for fellows to gain exposure to one of the world’s most influential countries.

India plays an increasingly important role in global diplomacy, economic affairs, security, technology, and international relations.

Professional experience in India can therefore help fellows develop a broader understanding of South Asian affairs and India’s role in the international system.

3. International Affairs Fellowship in Indonesia

The International Affairs Fellowship in Indonesia offers another overseas opportunity within CFR’s international affairs portfolio.

Indonesia is a major country in Southeast Asia and plays an important role in regional and international affairs.

For fellows interested in Southeast Asian geopolitics, international cooperation, economic relations, regional security, and diplomacy, an overseas fellowship experience in Indonesia could provide valuable exposure to perspectives that differ from those found in the United States.

4. International Affairs Fellowship in Japan

The International Affairs Fellowship in Japan provides an opportunity for fellows to broaden their knowledge of Japan and its position within international affairs.

Japan has an important role in Asian security, global economics, technology, diplomacy, and U.S. foreign policy.

An overseas experience in Japan can therefore be relevant to professionals seeking a stronger understanding of East Asian affairs and the relationships shaping the Indo-Pacific region.

5. Chung Mong-Koo International Affairs Fellowship in the Republic of Korea

The Chung Mong-Koo International Affairs Fellowship in the Republic of Korea is another specialized international opportunity listed among CFR’s overseas programs.

The Republic of Korea occupies a strategically significant position in East Asia. Issues involving regional security, economic relations, technology, diplomacy, and relations with the United States are all important components of the broader international environment surrounding the Korean Peninsula.

This fellowship provides another avenue through which fellows can gain exposure to international affairs outside the United States.

6. Robert A. Belfer International Affairs Fellowship in European Security

The Robert A. Belfer International Affairs Fellowship in European Security focuses specifically on European security.

Security issues in Europe have major implications for international relations, transatlantic cooperation, defense policy, diplomacy, and U.S. foreign policy.

Professionals interested in European security and related foreign policy questions may therefore find this fellowship particularly relevant to their professional development.

Domestic Fellowship Programs

CFR’s fellowship portfolio also includes domestic programs based in the United States.

These opportunities allow fellows to gain exposure to foreign policy and international affairs without necessarily participating in an overseas placement.

The domestic programs listed include the following:

1. International Affairs Fellowship

The International Affairs Fellowship provides an opportunity for professionals committed to foreign policy to broaden their perspectives through a fellowship experience.

The program is part of CFR’s broader mission of developing a stronger and more diverse foreign policy community in the United States.

2. Edward R. Murrow Press Fellowship

The Edward R. Murrow Press Fellowship is particularly relevant to professionals working in journalism and the press.

Journalists play an important role in explaining international developments to the public. Understanding foreign policy, diplomacy, global security, and international institutions can strengthen the quality and depth of reporting on international affairs.

The Murrow fellowship therefore represents an opportunity connected to the intersection of journalism and foreign policy.

3. Stanton Nuclear Security Fellowship

The Stanton Nuclear Security Fellowship focuses on nuclear security.

Nuclear weapons, proliferation, deterrence, arms control, and international security remain significant issues in global affairs.

A specialized fellowship in nuclear security can provide professional exposure for individuals interested in understanding and contributing to policy discussions surrounding these complex issues.

4. Technologist-in-Residence Fellowship

The Technologist-in-Residence Fellowship reflects the increasingly important relationship between technology and international affairs.

Technology is transforming diplomacy, national security, economic competition, communication, intelligence, and international relations.

Professionals with technology backgrounds can therefore contribute valuable technical perspectives to foreign policy discussions.

The fellowship provides a pathway for technological expertise to intersect with the foreign policy community.

Fellowships by Nomination Only

Not every CFR fellowship follows the same application process.

The information provided specifically identifies a group of fellowships that are available by nomination only.

These include:

  • Historian-in-Residence Fellowship
  • Military Fellowships
  • National Intelligence Fellowship
  • State Department Fellowship on Technology Diplomacy

Because these opportunities are identified as nomination-only programs, interested individuals should not assume that they can apply through the same process used for publicly accessible fellowship opportunities.

This distinction is important for prospective candidates because the application pathway can vary significantly between programs.

Historian-in-Residence Fellowship

The Historian-in-Residence Fellowship provides an opportunity associated with historical expertise and international affairs.

History is an important component of foreign policy because contemporary international relationships are often shaped by historical events, political decisions, conflicts, alliances, treaties, and institutional developments.

A historian working within a foreign policy environment can therefore contribute valuable context to discussions about international affairs.

Military Fellowships

CFR’s Military Fellowships provide another pathway for individuals with military backgrounds to engage with the foreign policy community.

Military experience can offer important perspectives on national security, defense, international conflict, strategic planning, and relations between military institutions and policymakers.

Because the fellowship is identified under CFR’s nomination-only category, interested candidates should carefully review the specific process and eligibility requirements applicable to the program.

National Intelligence Fellowship

The National Intelligence Fellowship is another specialized program within CFR’s fellowship portfolio.

Intelligence plays a central role in national security and foreign policy decision-making. Reliable intelligence can help policymakers understand international developments, assess threats, and make informed strategic decisions.

The fellowship therefore sits at the intersection of intelligence and foreign policy.

State Department Fellowship on Technology Diplomacy

The State Department Fellowship on Technology Diplomacy addresses the growing importance of technology in international relations.

Emerging technologies increasingly influence diplomacy, national security, economic competition, international cooperation, and relations between governments.

Technology diplomacy brings technical and policy perspectives together, making expertise in this area increasingly important to modern foreign policy.

The fellowship provides a specialized opportunity connected to this evolving field.

Who Is Eligible for CFR Fellowships?

Eligibility varies considerably between the individual Council on Foreign Relations fellowship programs.

The general fellowship information provided states that CFR fellowships offer opportunities for U.S. citizens with a demonstrated commitment to a career in foreign policy.

This means prospective candidates should pay close attention to both the general CFR fellowship requirements and the specific eligibility rules for the fellowship they are interested in.

Potential candidates may include professionals whose careers or academic interests are connected to areas such as:

  • Foreign policy
  • International affairs
  • Diplomacy
  • Journalism
  • National security
  • Nuclear security
  • Military affairs
  • Intelligence
  • Technology
  • Technology diplomacy
  • European security
  • International relations
  • Policymaking
  • History and international affairs

However, the exact qualifications, professional experience requirements, nomination procedures, and citizenship requirements can differ from one fellowship to another.

Are Applicants From Other Countries Eligible?

The general information supplied for the CFR fellowship portfolio specifically describes the opportunities as being for U.S. citizens with a demonstrated commitment to a career in foreign policy.

Therefore, applicants should not assume that simply being a resident of another country makes them eligible.

At the same time, CFR’s portfolio includes overseas fellowship programs in Canada, India, Indonesia, Japan, the Republic of Korea, and Europe. The location of a fellowship should not automatically be interpreted as meaning that citizens of that country or region can apply.

For example, the existence of an International Affairs Fellowship in India does not, based on the information provided alone, establish that all Indian citizens are eligible.

Applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Oceania, or other regions should therefore review the eligibility requirements of the specific fellowship before applying.

What Makes These Fellowships Different?

One of the distinguishing characteristics of the CFR fellowship portfolio is its emphasis on exposure to new environments.

Rather than limiting fellows to their existing professional setting, CFR seeks to provide selected participants with experiences that can broaden their understanding of foreign affairs.

This can involve exposure to:

  1. Policymaking environments
  2. CFR’s professional and research environment
  3. Overseas settings
  4. Journalism and media
  5. Military and national security perspectives
  6. Intelligence
  7. Nuclear security
  8. Technology and technology diplomacy
  9. Regional security
  10. International affairs research and policy discussions

Such exposure can help professionals develop a more comprehensive understanding of the factors that shape foreign policy.

Professional Development and Career Benefits

Participating in a prestigious foreign policy fellowship can contribute to professional growth in several ways.

Broader understanding of international affairs

Fellows can gain exposure to international issues beyond their existing area of expertise.

Exposure to policymaking

The opportunity to work in or around policymaking environments can provide insight into how foreign policy ideas are developed and implemented.

International experience

The overseas fellowship programs can expose fellows to international environments and perspectives.

Cross-sector learning

CFR’s portfolio covers journalism, technology, military affairs, intelligence, nuclear security, history, and diplomacy. This creates opportunities for professionals from different backgrounds to engage with foreign policy.

Professional network development

Working within a foreign policy environment can help fellows develop relationships with other professionals, researchers, policymakers, journalists, and experts.

Greater perspective

Exposure to different institutions and countries can help participants develop a broader understanding of international challenges.

Featured CFR Events and International Affairs Content

The Council on Foreign Relations fellowship page also highlights meetings, expert analysis, and reports related to international affairs.

Among the featured content listed in the provided information is the 2026 International Affairs Fellowship (IAF) Summer Series: Multilateralism Under Pressure, held on July 29, 2026.

The event reflects the type of foreign policy discussion associated with CFR’s broader work and highlights the importance of multilateralism in an increasingly complicated international environment.

The page also features analysis and reports addressing major global issues.

One featured expert take examines how rising deaths from earthquakes in Venezuela tested U.S. disaster relief.

Another article examines U.S. policy surrounding artificial intelligence oversight, demonstrating the growing intersection between technology and national policy.

A report on preventing renewed conflict in Colombia highlights the importance of conflict prevention and international engagement.

These topics demonstrate the breadth of issues connected to the broader foreign policy community.

Council on Foreign Relations and the U.S. Foreign Policy Community

Beyond its fellowship programs, the Council on Foreign Relations maintains a broader ecosystem focused on international affairs.

The CFR website provides access to areas including:

  • Membership
  • Fellowships
  • Careers
  • Newsletters
  • CFR Education
  • Events
  • Foreign policy analysis
  • Reports
  • Expert commentary
  • International affairs resources

The fellowship program forms part of this wider effort to strengthen the foreign policy community.

CFR also states that it is committed to fostering a foreign policy community in the United States that is more representative of American society as a whole.

This emphasis on representation is an important component of the organization’s fellowship mission.

How to Approach a CFR Fellowship Opportunity

Because CFR operates several different fellowship programs, prospective candidates should avoid treating the fellowship portfolio as a single application.

Instead, applicants should:

  1. Identify the fellowship that most closely matches their professional background and foreign policy interests.
  2. Read the specific eligibility requirements for that fellowship.
  3. Determine whether the program accepts direct applications or operates through nomination or invitation.
  4. Review the required application materials.
  5. Confirm citizenship and professional eligibility requirements.
  6. Check the fellowship’s specific deadline.
  7. Research the focus area of the fellowship.
  8. Prepare application materials that clearly demonstrate a commitment to foreign policy.
  9. Highlight relevant professional, academic, research, journalism, military, technology, or policy experience.
  10. Submit the application through the official CFR process where applicable.

Important Note About Application Deadlines

There is no single overall deadline stated in the information provided for all Council on Foreign Relations fellowships.

Instead, eligibility and application procedures vary among individual fellowship programs.

Applicants should therefore avoid relying on a general CFR fellowship deadline and should check the specific fellowship page for:

  • Opening date
  • Closing date
  • Eligibility requirements
  • Application procedure
  • Required documents
  • Nomination requirements
  • Citizenship requirements
  • Fellowship duration
  • Location
  • Selection criteria

This is particularly important because some fellowships are available by nomination or invitation only.

APPLY HERE

Who Should Consider Applying?

CFR fellowship opportunities may be especially relevant to professionals who have already developed a strong interest in international affairs and want to take the next step in their careers.

Potentially relevant candidates include professionals working in:

  • Government and public policy
  • Diplomacy and international relations
  • Journalism and media
  • National security
  • Defense
  • Intelligence
  • Technology
  • Nuclear security
  • International development
  • Research
  • Academia
  • History
  • Foreign policy analysis

Candidates should, however, evaluate their background against the specific requirements of the fellowship they are considering.

Why This Opportunity Can Be Valuable for a Foreign Policy Career

Foreign policy careers often require more than academic knowledge.

Professionals may need to understand how governments make decisions, how international institutions operate, how geopolitical relationships evolve, how journalists communicate global developments, how technological changes affect security, and how policymakers respond to emerging threats.

A fellowship that provides exposure to these environments can help bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical understanding.

For professionals committed to foreign policy, the opportunity to work in a new environment can also encourage new perspectives and challenge assumptions developed within a single institution or professional sector.

Final Thoughts

The Council on Foreign Relations Fellowships represent a diverse collection of professional development opportunities for individuals committed to foreign policy and international affairs.

From overseas International Affairs Fellowships in Canada, India, Indonesia, Japan, the Republic of Korea, and Europe to domestic programs focused on international affairs, journalism, nuclear security, and technology, CFR offers a broad fellowship portfolio addressing different aspects of modern foreign policy.

The organization also maintains specialized fellowships involving historians, military professionals, intelligence, and technology diplomacy, although some of these opportunities are available only through nomination or invitation.

For prospective candidates, one of the most important points to remember is that CFR fellowship eligibility is not uniform across every program. The general information identifies U.S. citizens with a demonstrated commitment to a career in foreign policy as the primary audience, but individual fellowships have their own requirements.

There is also no single overall deadline provided for the entire CFR fellowship portfolio. Candidates should therefore identify the specific fellowship they are interested in and verify its current deadline, eligibility requirements, application procedure, and whether direct applications are accepted.

For qualified professionals seeking to expand their foreign policy knowledge, gain exposure to policymaking or international environments, and develop a broader understanding of global affairs, a Council on Foreign Relations fellowship can represent a significant professional development opportunity.

item.content:encoded:
The Freedom Prize 2027 International Jury is inviting young people from France and around the world to apply for the opportunity to become one of 24 young international jury members responsible for identifying three individuals or organisations whose work represents an outstanding fight for freedom.

Open to young people aged 15 to 25, this unique youth participation opportunity offers applicants the chance to contribute to an international selection process, examine issues surrounding freedom and human rights, exchange perspectives with young people from different backgrounds, and participate in deliberations in Normandy, France.

The opportunity is particularly suitable for young people who are passionate about freedom, human rights, justice, peace, equality, civic engagement, advocacy, social change, and global issues.

Importantly, applicants do not need to have served on a jury before or possess a particular academic or professional background. The organisers state that the jury is open to both experienced and novice candidates and that particular attention will be given to applicants’ motivation and the diversity of profiles represented on the jury.

Applications for the international jury are open from June 4 to September 30, 2026.

What Is the Freedom Prize?

The Freedom Prize is an initiative that gives young people aged 15 to 25 the opportunity to identify and support inspiring individuals or organisations involved in exemplary struggles for freedom.

The programme is built around three major stages:

  1. The “Our Freedom Prize 2027” call for proposals
  2. The international jury deliberations
  3. The international online vote to select the laureate

The international jury plays a particularly important role because its 24 members will review proposals submitted through the Freedom Prize nomination process and collectively select three nominees.

Young people worldwide will then have the opportunity to vote online for one of these three nominees.

The eventual laureate will receive an endowment of €25,000 to support their ongoing fight for freedom.

Apply to Become a Member of the Freedom Prize 2027 International Jury

The international jury will consist of 24 young people between the ages of 15 and 25.

The organisers aim to make the jury representative of international youth and reflective of different cultural, geographical, and generational perspectives.

The jury will include young people representing three broad geographical levels:

  • Normandy
  • Other regions of France
  • Other countries around the world

This international composition is intended to bring different experiences, viewpoints, cultures, and understandings of freedom into the deliberations.

As a result, applicants from countries outside France are strongly relevant to the international dimension of the programme.

What Will International Jury Members Do?

Being selected for the Freedom Prize international jury is more than simply attending an event in France.

Jury members will actively participate in a structured process involving research, analysis, discussion, argumentation, individual reflection, and collaborative decision-making.

During the deliberations, members will examine proposals submitted through the “Our Freedom Prize 2027” call for nominations.

These proposals will identify individuals or organisations involved in significant struggles for freedom.

The jury’s responsibility will be to carefully consider these proposals and determine which fights are particularly representative of the concerns and aspirations of young people in relation to freedom in 2027.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Studying proposals submitted through the Freedom Prize call for nominations
  • Researching the individuals and organisations presented in the proposals
  • Analysing the different causes and struggles represented
  • Reflecting individually on the proposals
  • Participating in collaborative discussions
  • Presenting and defending arguments
  • Comparing different perspectives and points of view
  • Developing shared criteria for evaluating the different proposals
  • Participating in the final selection of three nominees

At the end of the deliberation process, the 24 jury members will collectively select three individuals or organisations whose fight they consider particularly representative of a fight for freedom in 2027.

These three nominees will then proceed to the public voting stage.

Three Key Stages of the Freedom Prize 2027

The Freedom Prize 2027 is structured around three major phases.

1. “Our Freedom Prize 2027” Call for Proposals

The first stage invites young people aged 15 to 25 from France and around the world to nominate an inspiring individual or organisation committed to a fight for freedom.

Applicants use an online form to present their nominee and explain why the person or organisation deserves recognition.

According to the opportunity information, the call for nominations will remain open until January 12, 2027.

For applicants to the international jury, completing this nomination form is a requirement. The form becomes available from September 1, 2026, and it can be submitted after the jury application if necessary.

This means prospective jury members should ensure that they complete the additional nomination requirement even if they initially submit their jury application before the nomination form becomes available.

2. International Jury Deliberations

The second stage involves the 24-member international jury meeting in Normandy.

The formal deliberation period is scheduled for February 15–19, 2027, while the broader jury stay in Normandy is scheduled for Sunday, February 14 through Saturday, February 20, 2027.

Applicants should therefore plan to be available for the entire February 14–20 period, rather than only the formal deliberation dates.

During this stage, jury members will meet, prepare for their responsibilities, study the proposals, exchange ideas, and ultimately select the three nominees for the Freedom Prize 2027.

The deliberations are facilitated by the International Institute for Human Rights and Peace.

A Chairperson will also participate in the process, helping guide the reflections and sharing their own testimony concerning freedom and commitment.

3. Online Vote for the Freedom Prize 2027

After the international jury selects three nominees, the process moves to an international online voting stage.

The voting period is scheduled for March 22 to April 30, 2027.

Young people aged 15 to 25 from around the world will be able to vote for their preferred nominee from the three individuals or organisations selected by the international jury.

The nominee receiving the winning support will become the Freedom Prize 2027 laureate.

The laureate will receive an endowment of €25,000 intended to support their ongoing fight for freedom.

The award ceremony is scheduled to take place in Caen, France, in June 2027.

International Jury Meeting in Normandy, France

One of the most significant aspects of this opportunity is the opportunity for selected jury members to meet physically in Normandy.

The international panel will meet in Normandy from Sunday, February 14 to Saturday, February 20, 2027.

Applicants must confirm that they are available during these dates before submitting their application.

The stay will allow jury members to:

  • Meet other young people from different backgrounds
  • Prepare for their responsibilities
  • Participate in the jury deliberations
  • Discuss different perspectives on freedom
  • Conduct research and analysis
  • Exchange ideas and arguments
  • Work collectively toward the selection of the three nominees

This makes the programme both a decision-making opportunity and an international youth exchange experience.

Travel, Accommodation, Food and Visa Costs Covered

Selected jury members will not be expected to personally finance the main costs associated with attending the February meeting in Normandy.

According to the opportunity information, the organisers will cover:

  • Transportation
  • Accommodation
  • Catering
  • Visa costs

This is an important benefit for international applicants, particularly those travelling from outside France.

Applicants should carefully follow any instructions provided by the organisers concerning travel arrangements, visa documentation, and other logistical requirements after selection.

Eligibility Requirements for the Freedom Prize 2027 Jury

Applicants should carefully review the eligibility conditions before applying.

Age Requirement

Applicants must be between 15 and 25 years old on February 19, 2027.

This is an essential requirement.

Being within the age range when applying is not enough if the applicant will no longer meet the age requirement on February 19, 2027.

Prospective applicants should therefore calculate their age on the specified date before submitting the application.

Worldwide Eligibility

The opportunity is open to young people from around the world.

The jury is deliberately designed to include young people representing different geographical areas, cultures, and generations.

The programme specifically refers to participation from:

  • Normandy
  • Other parts of France
  • Other countries around the world

Therefore, the opportunity is not restricted to applicants living in France.

Young people from African countries, Asian countries, European countries, countries in North and South America, Oceania, and other parts of the world can potentially apply, provided they satisfy the other eligibility requirements.

Language Requirements

Applicants must be able to express themselves orally and in writing in either French or English.

Applicants can choose either language.

No other language will be used for exchanges with the organisers or during the jury deliberations.

Therefore, applicants should be comfortable communicating, discussing ideas, presenting arguments, and participating in group conversations in either English or French.

Applicants do not need to demonstrate proficiency in both languages if they can adequately communicate in one of the two accepted languages.

No Specific Academic or Professional Background Required

One of the most inclusive aspects of the opportunity is that there is no requirement for a specific educational or professional background.

The jury welcomes candidates with different experiences and profiles.

You do not necessarily need to be:

  • A university student
  • A human rights professional
  • An activist
  • A researcher
  • A lawyer
  • A political science student
  • A journalist
  • A member of an organisation
  • An experienced youth leader

The organisers explicitly state that the jury is open to experienced and novice candidates.

This means that someone without previous experience in a similar programme can still apply.

The emphasis is instead placed on the applicant’s motivation and the overall diversity of the jury.

Previous Freedom Prize Jury Members Cannot Reapply

There is one specific restriction concerning previous participation.

A person who has already been a member of the Freedom Prize jury in a previous edition cannot stand for the jury again.

This condition is designed to help provide opportunities to new young people and maintain diversity among jury members.

Mandatory “Our Freedom Prize 2027” Nomination

Applicants for the international jury must also complete the “Our Freedom Prize 2027” call for nominations form.

The nomination involves proposing an individual or organisation that is engaged in a fight for freedom.

Importantly, the nomination form will be available from September 1, 2026.

The organisers indicate that the nomination form can be completed even if it is submitted after the jury application.

Applicants should therefore make sure they do not overlook this additional requirement.

A strong nomination should clearly identify the person or organisation being proposed and explain the importance and impact of their work in relation to freedom.

How Are International Jury Members Selected?

Selection is conducted by the organisers of the Freedom Prize.

The information provided in the application form will be considered when determining who is selected.

The organisers are particularly interested in ensuring diversity of profiles within the international jury.

This includes diversity in areas such as:

  • Geography
  • Culture
  • Generation
  • Experience
  • Personal background
  • Perspectives and viewpoints

The programme does not require applicants to have participated in similar initiatives before.

Instead, motivation is given particular attention.

The organisers may also conduct telephone interviews with applicants before making the final selection.

Applicants should therefore provide thoughtful and genuine responses throughout the application form and be prepared to discuss their motivation if contacted.

What Makes a Strong Applicant?

Although the organisers do not require a particular educational or professional background, applicants should demonstrate genuine interest in the purpose of the Freedom Prize.

A strong application could communicate:

  • Why freedom matters to you
  • Your understanding of freedom and human rights
  • Your interest in social or civic issues
  • Your ability to listen to perspectives different from your own
  • Your willingness to engage in constructive debate
  • Your ability to analyse information critically
  • Your interest in learning from other young people
  • Your ability to work collaboratively
  • Your motivation for joining the international jury
  • What perspective or experience you could contribute to a diverse international jury

Applicants should avoid presenting themselves simply as people looking for an opportunity to travel to France.

The jury has an important responsibility, so the application should demonstrate a genuine understanding of the role and its purpose.

Preparatory Work Before Travelling to France

Being selected does not mean that jury members can simply wait until February to participate.

Before travelling to Caen and Normandy, each international jury member agrees to:

  • Participate in preparatory video conferences
  • Complete preparation work remotely
  • Familiarise themselves with the jury’s responsibilities
  • Prepare for the deliberation process

Applicants should therefore be able to commit time to the programme before the physical meeting in February 2027.

This remote preparation is an important part of the overall experience.

Application Process

The application is structured into several sections.

Applicants are asked to complete the following stages:

  1. Presentation
  2. Contact details
  3. Languages
  4. Application
  5. Resume/CV

The application form allows candidates to choose between English and French.

Applicants should carefully complete each section and ensure that the information supplied is accurate and consistent.

A resume/CV must be attached at the end of the application.

Because motivation is an important consideration in the selection process, applicants should give serious attention to their written responses rather than treating the application as a simple registration form.

What Should You Prepare Before Applying?

Prospective applicants can prepare the following materials and information in advance.

1. An Updated CV

Your CV should clearly present relevant aspects of your background, interests, education, work, volunteering, leadership, community activities, projects, advocacy, or other experiences.

Because there is no required professional background, applicants should not assume that they need an extensive CV.

2. Your Motivation

Think carefully about why you want to become a member of the Freedom Prize international jury.

Consider:

  • Why are you interested in freedom?
  • Why do you want to participate in the selection process?
  • What perspectives can you contribute?
  • How do you approach disagreement?
  • What would you like to learn from other young people?
  • Why is international youth participation important?

3. Language Ability

Choose the language in which you can communicate most confidently: English or French.

4. Availability

Make sure you can commit to the required preparatory activities and the February 2027 stay in Normandy.

5. Your Freedom Prize Nomination

From September 1, 2026, make sure you complete the required “Our Freedom Prize 2027” nomination form.

Important Dates for the Freedom Prize 2027

The following dates are important for applicants:

  • International jury applications open: June 4, 2026
  • “Our Freedom Prize 2027” nomination form available: September 1, 2026
  • International jury application deadline: September 30, 2026
  • Nomination call deadline: January 12, 2027
  • Jury stay in Normandy: February 14–20, 2027
  • Formal jury deliberations: February 15–19, 2027
  • Online Freedom Prize vote: March 22–April 30, 2027
  • Freedom Prize award ceremony: June 2027

Freedom Prize 2027 Jury Application Deadline

The application must be validated online no later than Wednesday, September 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM Paris time, France.

Applications or confirmations submitted after the deadline will not be considered.

Applicants should therefore avoid waiting until the final hours to submit their forms.

Because the deadline is expressed in Paris time, international applicants should account for the time difference between France and their country when submitting their application.

What Happens After You Apply?

The organisers will assess applications based on the information provided.

The selection process is intended to create a diverse international jury rather than simply select applicants according to a single academic or professional criterion.

Some applicants may also be contacted for a telephone interview before the final selection.

Successful candidates will then participate in the preparatory activities and ultimately travel to Normandy for the February 2027 jury meeting.

Data Protection and Privacy

The application form also contains important information concerning the processing of applicants’ personal data.

The data collected is processed by the Normandy Region to assist with the organisation of the Freedom Prize.

The information may be shared with the organisers of the event and will be stored for ten years after the event.

Applicants are informed of their rights under the European data protection framework and French data protection legislation.

These rights include the ability to:

  • Access personal information
  • Request correction of personal information
  • Request deletion of personal information
  • Object to the processing of personal information

For matters relating to data protection, applicants can contact the Data Protection Officer at dpo@normandie.fr.

Applicants should also review the applicable rules and data-processing information before submitting the form.

Questions and Application Support

Applicants who experience difficulties completing the application or who have questions about participation can contact the Freedom Prize organisers.

The contact email provided for enquiries is:

prixliberte@normandie.fr

A text version of the application form is also available upon request for applicants who require it.

Why Young People Should Consider Applying

The Freedom Prize international jury offers young people an opportunity to take part in a meaningful international decision-making process.

Rather than simply attending a conference, jury members will have a direct role in evaluating proposals and identifying the three candidates who will proceed to the final public vote.

The experience can provide exposure to:

  • International youth participation
  • Human rights and freedom issues
  • Research and analysis
  • Argumentation
  • Collaborative decision-making
  • Cross-cultural dialogue
  • Public-interest advocacy
  • Leadership and civic engagement
  • International networking
  • Critical thinking
  • Group deliberation

For young people interested in international development, human rights, diplomacy, public policy, social change, advocacy, journalism, law, politics, peacebuilding, or community leadership, the experience may also provide valuable personal and professional development.

A Unique International Youth Experience

The international jury is designed around the idea that young people should have a meaningful role in determining which freedom-related struggles deserve international recognition.

The programme brings together 24 young people from different geographical and cultural backgrounds and gives them a shared responsibility.

Rather than requiring everyone to have identical experiences or opinions, the organisers are looking for diversity.

This makes the ability to listen, analyse, discuss, question assumptions, and work with people who have different perspectives particularly important.

The jury members will collectively determine which three causes are most representative of a fight for freedom in 2027.

Their decision will then shape the final stage of the Freedom Prize.

Official Application and Further Information

Applicants should review the official Freedom Prize information and rules before submitting their application.

Official website: https://prixliberte.normandie.fr/en

Applicants should ensure that they understand all participation requirements, particularly the age requirement, language requirement, February availability, previous-jury restriction, CV requirement, and mandatory “Our Freedom Prize 2027” nomination.

More global opportunities visit OFY Website HERE

Conclusion

The Freedom Prize 2027 International Jury offers young people aged 15 to 25 from around the world an opportunity to take an active role in an international process focused on freedom, human rights, commitment, and social change.

The selected jury will consist of 24 young people, bringing together different geographical, cultural, and generational perspectives. Members will study nominations, conduct research and analysis, exchange arguments, compare viewpoints, and collectively select three individuals or organisations whose fight for freedom they believe is particularly representative of young people’s concerns in 2027.

The opportunity does not require a specific degree, profession, or previous jury experience. Instead, the organisers place particular importance on applicants’ motivation and the diversity of profiles represented in the jury.

Selected members will participate in preparatory activities before travelling to Normandy, where they will take part in the February 2027 programme. Transportation, accommodation, catering, and visa costs will be covered by the organisers, making the opportunity accessible to selected participants from different parts of the world.

If you are between 15 and 25 on February 19, 2027, can communicate confidently in English or French, are interested in freedom and social issues, and are prepared to contribute thoughtfully to an international youth jury, this could be a valuable opportunity to consider.

Application deadline: Wednesday, September 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM Paris time, France.

Applicants should submit their applications well before the deadline and remember to complete the required “Our Freedom Prize 2027” nomination form, which becomes available on September 1, 2026.
